She learns the name of every garden flower and offers small bouquets to those she meets. Her gentle blossom breeze tends her companions' wounds and ailments.
ギリシャ神話の虹と伝令の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。雲と流水を織り込んだ袖が: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the rainbow and messenger goddess of Greek mythology. Clouds and flowing water grace sleeves that shimmer in soft rainbow colors. Carrying replies to the invitation with care, she shares stories from distant lands. In battle, she encourages her companions and clears away enemy enhancements.
海竜の姫が、深藍の絹と真珠のレースを纏って陸の月を見上げる。珊瑚の角と二筋の潮は: A sea-dragon princess gazes at the moon above the land, dressed in deep-blue silk and pearl lace. Coral horns and twin currents recall the sea palace she cannot return to. Water gathered in her shell cup embraces two wounded companions without distinction.
人の途絶えた機殿で、今日も朝の光を織り続ける女神。琥珀の髪に挿した小さな杼は、消: A goddess keeps weaving morning light in an abandoned weaving hall. A tiny shuttle in her amber hair binds fading wishes anew. Gold thread edging her black lace draws out her companions' strength, while a soft woven ward receives approaching blades.
花の散った後も山を守る、永い命の女神。翡翠の瞳と短い石灰色の髪、重たい黒の衣に小: A goddess of enduring life guards the mountains after the blossoms fall. Small alpine flowers adorn her heavy black dress, beneath jade eyes and short limestone-gray hair. She transforms memories of rejection into a shield for her companions and a stone scepter that breaks false barriers.
生と黄泉の境に架かる橋で、こじれた願いの結び目をほどく女神。銅赤の三つ編みと水引: On a bridge between life and the underworld, a goddess gently untangles knotted wishes. The silver scissors in her copper-red braid are not meant to sever bonds. She loosens only the threads of enemy power and regeneration, opening a path for her companions.

忘れても、約束はここに。: Even if I forget, the promise remains here.
セリス……一緒に、帰りましょう。: Seris… let us go home together.
命令より、帰る者を守る。: I protect those returning home, above any order.
帰還の許可なら、とうに出ている。: Permission to return was granted long ago.

……最後の稽古は、隣を歩くことにしましょう。: …For our final lesson, let us walk side by side.
あの日の剣を、今度こそ越えて。: This time, surpass the sword of that day.
ひとりで夜を引き受けるのは、もう終わり。: You no longer have to bear the night alone.
約束の朝へ。一緒に、帰ろう。: Toward the promised dawn. Let us go home together.
弔鐘の剣姫: Sword Maiden of the Passing Bell
セリスに剣を教えた女性。割れた鐘の耳飾りを揺らし、夜明けへの道を塞ぐ。あの子に教: The woman who taught Seris the sword blocks the way to dawn, a cracked bell earring swaying. There is one stance she never taught her pupil: how to stop someone returning home without cutting them down.
余分な一輪は弔いではなく、帰還の約束だった。白花を携え、今度は自分も朝へ向かう。: The extra flower was a promise of return, never an offering of mourning. Carrying white blossoms, she now walks toward morning herself.
盾のひびを金で継ぎ、門の外で仲間を待つ騎士。守るべきものを、自分の意志で選び直し: A knight waits outside the gate, the cracks in her shield mended with gold. She has chosen anew, of her own will, what she will protect.
星図の余白に、共に歩む者たちの名を書き足した。誰か一人を代償にする計算は、もう必: She added the names of her fellow travelers to the margins of her star chart. No calculation need demand a single person's sacrifice anymore.
弟子を夜に留める剣を下ろし、隣を歩く師。金で継いだ鐘は、弔いではなく朝の合図にな: The teacher lowers the sword that kept her pupil in the night and walks beside her. The bell mended with gold now signals morning, not mourning.
雨上がりの石畳を、彼女はもう懐かしそうには眺めない。その先へ、一緒に歩く人がいる: She no longer gazes at the rain-washed cobblestones with longing. Someone is there to walk with her beyond them.
薄明の剣と、約束の朝: The Twilight Sword and the Promised Dawn
四つの記憶が、夜の向こうで彼女を待つ。: Four memories await her beyond the night.
朝の来ない街で剣を振るう旅人。雨上がりの石畳を、いつも懐かしそうに眺めている。彼: A traveler wields her sword in a city where morning never comes. She gazes at rain-washed cobblestones with longing. A single crack darker than night runs through her blade.
礼拝堂の白花、門の鍵、星図の余白、遠い鐘。知らないはずのものに触れるたび、剣を握: White flowers in the chapel, a gate key, the margins of a star chart, a distant bell. Whenever she touches something she should not recognize, her sword hand stills. "I feel as though I promised someone we would go home together."
街が滅びる朝を、彼女は剣で切り離した。人々を守った夜は、やがて名前まで奪っていっ: With her sword, she cut away the morning that would destroy the city. The night that protected its people eventually stole even their names. The four companions recovered no miracle, but a promise to face tomorrow together. She no longer gazes at rain-washed cobblestones with longing. Someone is there to walk with her beyond them.
礼拝堂の花は、いつも一輪だけ多い。誰のためか尋ねると、彼女は旅人の剣を見た。: There is always one extra flower in the chapel. Asked whom it is for, she looks at the traveler's sword.
旅立ちの日、エレインはセリスに花を渡さなかった。「帰ったら、一緒に摘みましょう」: On the day they departed, Elaine gave Seris no flower. "When we return, let us pick them together." Those words alone keep returning to her lips in the middle of prayer.
朝を封じに行くセリスを、彼女は止められなかった。だから残した一輪は弔いではない。: She could not stop Seris from going to seal away morning. The flower she left was therefore no token of mourning. "This time, I am coming too. So we remember the flowers' names on our way home." For the first time, the white blossom awaits morning dew.
門を破った傷は、外側にはひとつもない。錆銀の騎士は、鍵を誰にも預けない。: There is not a single mark of the breached gate on its outer side. The tarnished-silver knight entrusts its key to no one.
最後の勅命は、城門を閉ざすことだった。リオラはその命令書を盾の裏に隠している。折: The final royal command was to close the city gate. Liora keeps the order hidden behind her shield. Beyond its folds, only Seris's footprints remain.
あの夜、門を内側から開いたのはリオラだった。王国への誓いより、帰ってくる一人を選: That night, Liora opened the gate from within. Over her oath to the kingdom, she chose the one person who would return. Raising her shield mended with gold, she waits for Seris outside the gate this time. "Permission to return was granted long ago."
彼女の本には、一夜分だけ朝の記録がある。末尾の名前は、何度も書き直されていた。: Her book contains a record of morning for just one night. The name at its end has been rewritten many times.
星図に朝を描くたび、同じ場所のインクが消える。ノエルはそこにセリスの名を書き、消: Whenever she draws morning onto the star chart, the ink in the same place fades. Noelle writes Seris's name there and reads it aloud before it vanishes.
封印を解けば、街は止められていた滅びと再び向き合う。ノエルはそれを知り、一人に代: Breaking the seal means facing the destruction that was held at bay. Knowing this, Noelle abandoned any calculation that would demand one person's sacrifice. When she added four names to the star chart's margins, the vanished morning star returned.

弟子に街の命運を背負わせたまま、師は夜の終わりを恐れていた。弔鐘のひびを金で継ぎ: Having left the city's fate on her pupil's shoulders, the teacher feared the night's end. Mending the passing bell with gold, Lisette lowered her sword. "Your final lesson. This time, walk beside me." The bell now signals morning, not mourning.
白霧の足跡は、礼拝堂から門へ続く。: White-mist pawprints lead from the chapel to the gate.
狼は紺の外套の裾を嗅ぐと、雨上がりの道に伏せた。帰る者を待つ仕草だった。: The wolf sniffed the hem of the navy cloak, then lay down on the rain-washed road. It was waiting for someone to return.
霧の向こうに、まだ名を呼ぶ声が残っている。: Beyond the mist, a voice still calls a name.
枯園の荊には、白い布の切れ端が結ばれている。: A scrap of white cloth is tied to a thorn in the withered garden.
「あの剣が朝を斬った日から、種は芽を出す夢ばかり見る」。魔女は新しい鉢を窓辺に置: "Since that sword cut away morning, the seeds dream only of sprouting." The witch placed a new pot by the window.

瀬織津姫を着想にした、急流と祓いの女神。氷青の長髪に紙垂を結び、黒と白の礼装で朽: Inspired by Seoritsuhime, goddess of purification and swift rivers. 弥都波能売神を着想にした、水の女神。紺の短い髪に雨粒の銀飾りを挿し、薄紫と黒の裾: Inspired by Mizuhanome, goddess of water. A silver raindrop pin glints in her short navy hair as her lavender and black skirts brush an ancient bridge. 埴安姫神を着想にした、土と粘土の女神。栗色の横結びと深紅の工房服、金継ぎの走る陶: Inspired by Haniyasuhime, goddess of earth and clay. ギリシャ神話の狩猟の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。長い銀の三つ編みに三日月を挿: Inspired by Artemis, Greek goddess of the hunt, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. ギリシャ神話の春と冥府の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。黒いボブに一筋の紅、葡萄: Inspired by Persephone, Greek goddess of spring and the underworld, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. A crimson streak marks her black bob, and white flowers mingle with roots along her wine-red hem. The pomegranate in her palm is a light to remember the way home. At the border of spring and night, she unravels enemy defenses and borrows a thread of life to stand once more.

ギリシャ神話の炉の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。銅赤の髪を低く結び、生成りの小: Inspired by Hestia, Greek goddess of the hearth, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. With copper hair in a low bun, an ivory kimono, and a charcoal haori, she cradles a little lantern. At the edge of the gathering, she is the first to bring warmth to cold hands. Her sheltering back and barriers of lamplight keep a place open for everyone to return.
ギリシャ神話の青春と給仕の女神を着想にした、成人の姿の客人。淡い桃色の髪を高く結: Inspired by Hebe, Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods, portrayed as an adult guest. Her pale pink hair is tied high above an aqua kimono woven with white cranes as she carries a single cup. She celebrates the courage to take a new step. Her healing cup mends one deep wound, or lets two companions share its comfort for lighter injuries.
月白の衣と銀の飾りを纏い、夜の道を照らす女神。花宴の振袖をしまった日も、仲間を気: Dressed in moon-white cloth and silver ornaments, she lights the roads of night. Even with her banquet furisode put away, her concern for her companions is unchanged. She shares a quiet glow with the wounded and gently guides them somewhere to rest. This is her everyday travelling attire in the world of STILLVEIL.
白い衣に軽い銀の鎧を重ね、梟とともに廃都の地図を読む女神。花宴の華やかな装いとは: Wearing light silver armor over white cloth, she studies the ruined city with an owl at her side. She greets companions in practical travelling clothes rather than her elaborate banquet attire. Reading an enemy's defenses, she chooses a path the party can safely follow. To her, wisdom is a means of protecting someone.
生成りと若草色の素朴なドレスで、朝の庭を手入れする女神。晴れ着を着ない日には、小: In a simple cream and soft green dress, she tends the morning garden. On days without festive clothes, she walks with a little basket of flowers. When she notices someone's wounds or weariness, she chooses a wildflower just for them. Her gentle work continues far beyond the banquet.
白と朱の端正な衣に、小さな日輪の飾りを添えた女神。特別なレースの衣装を離れ、いつ: In an elegant white and vermilion robe with a small sun ornament, she carries the morning light to her companions with her familiar mirror. Away from her special lace costume, she values enough light to see the road ahead over a dazzling display. This is her peaceful travelling form in the world of STILLVEIL.
墨色と生成りの長衣を纏い、静かな水辺に灯をともす女神。特別な黒いレースを脱いでも: In a flowing charcoal and ivory robe, she lights a lantern beside still water. Without her special black lace, her care for travellers remains unchanged. She calms the enemy's momentum and gives her companions a moment to breathe. This peaceful interpretation in the world of STILLVEIL pairs a gentle expression with quiet dignity.

銀の三つ編みを揺らし、森の小径を歩く女神。いつもの緑の旅装に弓を携え、獣の足跡か: With her silver braid and familiar green travel clothes, she follows forest paths with a bow at her side. Animal tracks show her the safest way through the ruins. When her companions lose their way at night, she leaves a little light before offering a word.
黒い短髪に小さな柘榴の飾りを添えた女神。深紅の旅衣で枯れた庭を巡り、まだ眠ってい: A small pomegranate ornament rests in her short black hair. In a burgundy travelling dress, she gathers sleeping seeds from abandoned gardens. 桃色の髪を高く結び、青い旅衣で水辺を歩く女神。休憩のたびに小さな茶器を取り出し、: Her pink ponytail bobs above a blue travelling dress as she walks beside the water. At every rest stop, she unpacks a little tea set and offers a warm cup. This dependable travelling companion reaches out to two wounded friends at once.

うさぎたちの行進が、静かな庭を起こす。: A parade of rabbits wakes the silent garden.

ま、負けてないし……もう一回、遊んでくれる？: I-I didn't lose... Will you play with me again?

Surrounded by her handmade mechanical rabbits, she invites passing travellers to play. She has long been waiting for a promise to go home together.

Star gears adorn her navy and ivory travelling clothes as she promises never to leave anyone behind. Even her cheeky laughter becomes a way to make sure her companions are still close.

灯りを失った回廊に、ごく稀に現れる銀髪の旅人。銀灯に集まる蛾は、帰り道を忘れた願: A silver-haired traveler rarely seen in unlit corridors. The moths gathering at her lantern are wishes that have forgotten the way home. “May I walk beside you until your morning comes?” The wick she offers still holds the warmth of a distant bell.

月の静けさの中で、あなたの歩みを見せて。: Show me your resolve in the stillness of moonlight.
まだ、夜は終わりません。: The night is not over yet.
どうぞ、そのまま次の光へ。: Go on, toward the next light.

ふふ……まだ帰すわけにはいかないの。: Hehe... I cannot let you leave just yet.
あなたの絆は、黄泉にもほどけなかった。: Even the underworld could not unravel your bonds.
最後は私！ あなたの光を、見せて！: I am your final challenge! Show me your light!
もっと輝けるよね。私も負けない！: You can shine brighter, right? I will not give in!
まぶしいね……その強さ、確かに届いたよ！: How dazzling... I felt your strength!

朝の来ない街に着いた。白霧の狼が、壊れた礼拝堂を振り返っている。: You arrive in a city without morning. A white wolf looks back toward a ruined chapel.

狼の足跡を追う。消えたはずの街灯が、一つずつ灯っていく。: You follow the wolf. Streetlamps thought dead begin to glow.
灯は人を迎えるためではない。庭の眠りを乱す者を数えていた。: The lights are not welcoming visitors. They are counting intruders.
鳴らない鐘の下で、古い地図を拾う。泉の位置だけが削り取られていた。: Beneath a silent bell, you find a map with its fountain scratched out.
地図の裏に「水音を辿るな」とある。階段の先から、水音がした。: The back reads: Do not follow the water. Beyond the stairs, water murmurs.
月の蛾が、閉じた花の上を渡る。狼は庭の入口で待つことを選んだ。: Moon moths drift above closed flowers. The wolf waits at the garden entrance.
花の根には青い石が絡んでいる。これは庭ではなく、何かを眠らせる蓋だった。: Blue stone binds the roots. This garden is a lid keeping something asleep.
水路を塞ぐ根を外す。石の奥から、ゆっくりした鼓動が聞こえる。: You clear roots from the channel. A slow heartbeat sounds inside the stone.
鼓動に合わせて水が引いた。泉へ向かう通路が現れる。: Water recedes with each heartbeat, revealing a passage toward the fountain.
濡れた祭具室に、人の手で直された花瓶が並ぶ。: In the flooded vestry, carefully repaired vases stand in rows.
小さな竜の彫像に、花を守る誓いが刻まれていた。: A small dragon statue bears an oath to protect the flowers.
青い灯を追うほど、足元の石が鱗に似てくる。: As you follow blue lanterns, the paving stones begin to resemble scales.
道そのものが、眠る竜の背を覆っていた。もう引き返すにも、その上を歩くしかない。: The path covers a sleeping dragon. Even retreat would mean walking across its back.
東屋の錠を外すと、長いあいだ閉じ込められた花の香りがした。: Opening the arbor releases the scent of flowers sealed away for years.
手記には「眠りが終われば庭も枯れる」とあった。守ることと止めることは、同じではな: A journal warns that the garden will wither when the sleep ends. Preservation is not the same as life.
泉へ続く橋が身じろぎする。石鱗の守り手は、侵入者の数を知っている。: The bridge shifts beneath you. The guardian knows how many intruders have come.
橋を渡りきると、狼が初めて小さく吠えた。逃げろという声ではなかった。: Once you cross, the wolf gives a quiet bark. It is not telling you to run.
枯れた苗の間に、ひと鉢だけ新しい芽がある。: Among dead seedlings, one pot holds a fresh shoot.
竜は庭を守ったが、次の季節を知らない。この芽を外へ運ぼう。: The dragon protected its garden but never saw another season. You take the seedling outside.
水面に大きな影が浮く。仲間は回復薬と盾を確かめた。: A vast shadow rises beneath the water. Your companions check their shields and medicines.
三度目の鼓動で石鱗が開く。大きな突進の後にこそ、攻める隙がある。: On the third beat, the scales part. A great charge will leave an opening.

中庭の荊をほどきながら、二人は恋人としての最初の約束をする。無理な日は、無理だと: Untangling the courtyard thorns, you make your first promise as lovers: say when something is too much.
「あなたが帰る場所になりたい。でも、それだけの人にはなりたくない」。彼女は自分の: “I want to be somewhere you can return to. But I want to be more than that.” She adds a little chair beside her research desk.
古い設計図が見つかる。二人の記憶を種に、自分の意思を持つ新しい個体を育てる培養炉: You discover plans for an incubator that can grow a new individual, with a will of its own, from two people’s memories. She calls it “our family.”
二人で安全装置を確かめ、最初の記憶を渡す。茶碗を選んだ午後。小さな核が、淡く光っ: Together you check its safeguards and offer a first memory: the afternoon you chose the teacups. A tiny core glows.
核は声に反応する。でも同じ挨拶しか返さない。彼女は「まだ足りないのかな」と手帳を: The core answers voices but repeats the same greeting. “Perhaps it needs more,” she says, opening her notebook.
計測値は安定している。それでも、彼女は茶碗を買った店を思い出せなくなっていた。あ: The readings are stable, yet she can no longer remember the shop where you bought the cups. You stop looking for reasons to halt the experiment.
診療室で、記憶の欠落は培養炉の負荷だと告げられる。療養を続け、実験を休止するよう: At the clinic, you learn the missing memories are caused by the incubator’s strain. The clinician recommends continued care and a pause in the experiment.
帰り道、彼女は休むと約束した。夜、あなたは炉の灯を見た。そして扉を叩かなかった。: She promises to rest. That night, you see the furnace glowing. You do not knock.

彼女は泣きながら笑った。「この子は、私を忘れない」。停止レバーには、いつの間にか: She laughs through tears. “This one will never forget me.” Someone has locked the shutdown lever.
彼女はあなたを別の名で呼んだ。炉を止めようとすると、怯えて設計図を抱え込む。: She calls you by another name. When you reach for the shutdown, she clutches the plans in fear.
「ここまで失くしたのに、何も生まれなかったことにしないで」。あなたは鍵を受け取れ: “After everything I have lost, do not make it all for nothing.” You cannot get the key. Even “I love you” no longer reaches her.
記録紙に同じ一日が何百回も並ぶ。炉は個体を育てず、二人の記憶を複製して自分を保っ: The records repeat a single day hundreds of times. The furnace is sustaining itself with copies of your memories instead of growing a new life.
彼女は眠れず、場所も時間も分からなくなった。あなたが救援を呼ぶ間に、炉は街の封印: Unable to sleep, she loses track of place and time. While you call for help, the furnace begins consuming the city’s seal.
リオラが温室を封鎖した。彼女を避難させたが、暴走した炉へ近づく者を、門の防衛機構: Liora seals the greenhouse and evacuates the witch. The gate’s defense system now treats anyone approaching the runaway furnace as an enemy.
「私が盾で機構を引き受ける。その間に止めろ」。炉を止めても、奪われた記憶は戻らな: “I will take the system into my shield. Stop it while you can.” Shutting down cannot restore the stolen memories. You take the final key.
防衛機構に操られたリオラの盾を越え、炉を止める。今度こそ、失うのが怖いという理由: You must break through Liora’s shield, seized by the defense system, and halt the furnace. Fear of losing her cannot delay you again.
炉は止まった。個体は生まれず、殻があなたの声で「おかえり」と繰り返す。療養室の彼: The furnace stops. No new life is born. Its shell repeats “Welcome home” in your voice. In the care room, she stares through the window and asks, “Who are you?” You take both cups home. Next morning, your voice calls again from the empty greenhouse.
温室から離れても、あの声が耳に残る。セリスは何も尋ねず、地下墓所への灯を持った。: Away from the greenhouse, that voice still follows you. Seris asks nothing and carries a lamp toward the crypt.
死者の名前には朝の日付がない。この街全体が、終われなかった日の中にいる。: None of the names of the dead has a morning date. The entire city remains inside a day that never ended.
名前の削られた墓を辿る。忘れたからといって、起きたことまで消えはしない。: You walk among graves whose names were erased. Forgetting does not undo what happened.
墓標の裏には、朝を斬った剣の紋があった。セリスは長く目を閉じた。: The reverse of a stone bears the sword that severed morning. Seris closes her eyes for a long time.

拾った紙には、封印を解く代償が残っていた。止めていた滅びも、動き出す。: A scrap names the price of ending the seal: the ruin it held back will move again.
灰の中でノエルの筆跡を探す。答えを知れば、救えるという保証はない。: You search the ashes for Noelle’s handwriting. Knowing the answer promises no rescue.
計算は一人の犠牲を必要としていた。余白に、別の手で「本当に？」と書かれている。: The calculation demands one sacrifice. In another hand, the margin asks: Must it?
一通だけ燃え残った手紙に、四人の名が並んでいた。: One surviving letter lists four names.
「ひとりに返さない」。書き手は、答えより先に約束を残した。: “We will not leave it to one person.” The writer left a promise before finding an answer.

空に星はない。それでもノエルは、観測をやめていなかった。: There are no stars. Noelle has kept observing anyway.
星が消えたのではない。街の夜だけが、空から切り離されている。: The stars are not gone. The city’s night has been severed from the sky.
星図の消えた部分に、仲間の名を書き直す。: You write your companions’ names onto the erased portions of the chart.
四つの名が消えずに残った。独りで支えるための式が、初めて崩れる。: Four names remain. The formula that required one person to bear everything finally breaks.
ノエルが星図を抱えて道を塞ぐ。希望だけで封印を解くなら、ここは通せないという。: Noelle bars the way with her chart. Hope alone is no reason to break the seal.
危険を引き受ける名を、全員が自分で書いた。彼女はようやく、鍵を差し出す。: Each of you writes your own name to accept the risk. At last, she offers the key.
夜明けを閉じ込めた水門を開く。取り戻せないものまで戻るわけではない。: You open the sluice that holds back dawn. It cannot return everything you have lost.
遠くの療養室にも、薄い光が入った。彼女があなたを思い出したという知らせは、来ない: A little light reaches the distant care room. No word comes that she remembers you.
リゼットが最後の道で待つ。「失う覚悟と、誰かを見捨てることを混同しないで」: Lisette waits on the final path. “Do not confuse accepting loss with abandoning someone.”
セリスは剣を抜く。正しい結末を貰うためではなく、選んだ明日を引き受けるために。: Seris draws her sword, to accept the tomorrow she chooses rather than earn a perfect ending.
弔鐘の剣姫を越え、街の朝を解き放つ。誰か一人を代償にはしない。: You face the swordswoman of the mourning bell and release the city’s morning. No one person will pay its price.
街に朝が来る。温室の椅子は空のままだった。あなたは茶碗を洗い、今日は扉を叩く。返: Morning reaches the city. The greenhouse chair remains empty. You wash the cups. Today you knock, to let her know you are there, even if no answer comes.
恋と、まだ生まれない命。戻せない記憶の物語。: Love, a life yet to be born, and memories that cannot return.
盾が、もう私の命令を聞かない……今のうちに、止めろ。: My shield no longer obeys me... Stop it while you can.
まだ意識はある。迷うな、炉へ行け！: I am still here. Do not hesitate. Get to the furnace!
朝の来ない街に着いた。: You arrive in a city without morning.
鳴らない鐘の下で、古い地図を拾う。: Beneath a silent bell, you find a map with its fountain scratched out.
月の蛾が、閉じた花の上を渡る。: Moon moths drift above closed flowers.
水路を塞ぐ根を外す。: You clear roots from the channel.
水面に大きな影が浮く。: A vast shadow rises beneath the water.
雨の日、あなたは食事を届ける。: On a rainy day, you bring a meal.
棚に二つ目の茶碗が置かれる。: A second teacup appears on the shelf.
中庭の荊をほどきながら、二人は恋人としての最初の約束をする。: Untangling the courtyard thorns, you make your first promise as lovers: say when something is too much.
古い設計図が見つかる。: You discover plans for an incubator that can grow a new individual, with a will of its own, from two people’s memories.
核は声に反応する。: The core answers voices but repeats the same greeting.
診療室で、記憶の欠落は培養炉の負荷だと告げられる。: At the clinic, you learn the missing memories are caused by the incubator’s strain.
培養槽があなたの声で彼女を呼ぶ。: The vessel calls to her in your voice.
彼女はあなたを別の名で呼んだ。: She calls you by another name.
記録紙に同じ一日が何百回も並ぶ。: The records repeat a single day hundreds of times.
リオラが温室を封鎖した。: Liora seals the greenhouse and evacuates the witch.
防衛機構に操られたリオラの盾を越え、炉を止める。: You must break through Liora’s shield, seized by the defense system, and halt the furnace.
温室から離れても、あの声が耳に残る。: Away from the greenhouse, that voice still follows you.
名前の削られた墓を辿る。: You walk among graves whose names were erased.
煤の足跡が書庫へ続く。: Sooty footprints lead toward the library.
灰の中でノエルの筆跡を探す。: You search the ashes for Noelle’s handwriting.
ノエルが星図を抱えて道を塞ぐ。: Noelle bars the way with her chart.
夜明けを閉じ込めた水門を開く。: You open the sluice that holds back dawn.

定数100。今は、届かなくてもいい。: Difficulty 100. Beyond your reach, for now.

守る一手、砕く一手。: One move to protect. One move to break.
セレネとアテナに挑む2連戦。攻撃重視では有効な障壁破壊・強化解除、生存重視では守: Two battles against Selene and Athena. Offense prioritizes useful barrier breaking and dispelling; survival favors protection and healing. Critically wounded allies remain protected. Prepare for a heavy strike every third turn and exploit the opening as the boss releases her barrier. No loot; healing items used are consumed.
SSRの排出対象が不足しています。石は消費されません。: No eligible SSR characters are available. No stones have been spent.
三つの道が交わる廃都の片隅で、蒼い灯火を絶やさない女神。腰の鍵は閉ざされた門では: At a crossroads in the ruined city, this goddess keeps three blue flames alight. The keys at her waist open a way out of troubled hearts rather than locked gates. She quietly unravels enemy blessings and watches from a little distance until each traveler chooses their own path.
鷹羽の外套と琥珀の首飾りを纏い、二匹の猫と忘れられた北の庭を巡る女神。美しいもの: Clad in falcon feathers and an amber necklace, she wanders forgotten northern gardens with two cats. Her love of beauty has taught her the pain of loss. "We can build a place to return to together." Even wounded, her hand never falters before the next strike.
水辺の朽ちた社で、誰も忘れた歌を琵琶に託す女神。ひとつの音が波紋になるたび、離れ: In a weathered waterside shrine, she entrusts forgotten songs to her biwa. Each note sends ripples of comfort to distant, wounded hearts. She prefers a quiet night beside weary travelers to a splendid feast, and stays until the final note fades.
長い水色の髪を夜風にほどき、滝から滝へ祈りを運ぶ女神。簡素な旅衣と銀の水鉢だけを: Her long blue hair catches the night breeze as she carries prayers between waterfalls. With simple traveling robes and a silver water bowl, she washes away her companions' ailments. She never tells them what awaits beyond the bridge, but walks beside them until they cross.
織りかけの朝を小さな糸巻きに収め、廃都を歩く女神。いつもの生成りの旅衣には、仲間: She carries an unfinished dawn on a small spool as she walks the ruined city. Her plain traveling dress bears stitches lovingly repaired by companions. Each gentle knot reminds them that they can continue their journey without haste.
稲穂と小さな升を抱え、白狐と里の跡を巡る女神。普段の旅衣は土の色に近く、畦道に座: With rice stalks and a little wooden measure, she visits abandoned villages alongside a white fox. Her earth-colored robes are made for resting on field paths. She shares the remaining harvest fairly and lays a thin ward over her companions before quietly taking her own portion.
